messages.text: 'Out in the middle of nowhere' - Hamilton rues Ferrari's handling of qualifying

metadata.summary: Lewis Hamilton felt Ferrari’s execution of the final stage of Italian Grand Prix qualifying had been "pretty bad" after the home team’s hopes of being able to challenge for pole position on Saturday fell flat.
metadata.content: Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari driver says team's execution of Italian GP qualifying could have been better after 'very tough' session | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari driver says team's execution of Italian GP qualifying could have been better after 'very tough' session Lewis Hamilton almost dropped out in Q2 before going on to finish fifth fastest in Q3, which became fourth on the grid behind team-mate Charles Leclerc; watch the Italian Grand Prix live on Sunday at 2pm on Sky Sports F1, with build-up from 12.30pm Saturday 5 September 2026 19:18, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc reflect on Ferrari's frustrating lack of pace during qualifying at the Italian Grand Prix in Monza. Lewis Hamilton felt Ferrari’s execution of the final stage of Italian Grand Prix qualifying had been "pretty bad" after the home team’s hopes of being able to challenge for pole position on Saturday fell flat. Ferrari had been tipped to contend for pole at their home Monza race but never truly appeared in the hunt at any stage of the knockout sessions with the Scuderia eventually outpaced in Q3 by three Mercedes-powered cars - including Alpine surprise polesitter Pierre Gasly. Oscar Piastri's later three-place grid penalty means Charles Leclerc and Hamilton will still both start on the second row in third and fourth places respectively. After Durham got up to 261 in their second innings to set a victory target of 204 at the start of day four, Callum Parkinson raced through the hosts' batting line-up in stunning fashion on his way to six for 20. Stokes then finished the job when he had the last laugh on Yuzvendra Chahal, who had dismissed the former England captain with a wonder delivery in the first innings, but was caught behind for 10 with Northamptonshire dismissed for only 50. messages.text: From Monaco 'robbery' to shock pole - but can Gasly win Italian GP?

metadata.summary: Pierre Gasly felt he was "robbed" on Friday after losing his podium from June's Monaco Grand Prix but turned it around in the most remarkable fashion with pole position for the Italian Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Italian GP: Can Pierre Gasly win Monza race for Alpine just days after losing Monaco podium? | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Italian GP: Can Pierre Gasly win Monza race for Alpine just days after losing Monaco podium? Pierre Gasly claimed a shock pole position just one day after losing his Monaco Grand Prix podium; Gasly starts alongside George Russell for what could be a thrilling race; watch the Italian Grand Prix live on Sunday at 2pm on Sky Sports F1, with build-up from 12.30pm Nigel Chiu Sports Journalist @NigelCJourno Saturday 5 September 2026 18:45, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from qualifying for the 2026 Italian Grand Prix Pierre Gasly felt he was "robbed" on Friday after losing his podium from June's Monaco Grand Prix but turned it around in the most remarkable fashion with pole position for the Italian Grand Prix. Just one day after the FIA International Court of Appeal reinstated Gasly's pit lane speeding penalties , the Alpine driver hit back with his maiden Formula 1 pole. It is one of the biggest shocks in the history of F1 and, six years after winning his only race to date, also coming at Monza, Gasly has the opportunity to avenge, what he feels, was a wrong judgement call on Friday. messages.text: 'He got done over by Max' - Wolff blames Verstappen for Russell losing pole

metadata.summary: Mercedes boss Toto Wolff has claimed that George Russell missed out on pole position for the Italian Grand Prix because he "got done over" by Max Verstappen during the closing stages of qualifying at Monza.
metadata.content: Mercedes boss Toto Wolff blames Max Verstappen for George Russell missing out on Italian GP pole to Pierre Gasly | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Exclusive Mercedes boss Toto Wolff blames Max Verstappen for George Russell missing out on Italian GP pole to Pierre Gasly George Russell missed out on pole as Pierre Gasly claimed a shock result for Alpine; Russell's final qualifying lap appeared to be compromised by Max Verstappen; watch the Italian Grand Prix live on Sunday at 2pm on Sky Sports F1, with build-up from 12.30pm Saturday 5 September 2026 18:47, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from qualifying for the 2026 Italian Grand Prix Mercedes boss Toto Wolff has claimed that George Russell missed out on pole position for the Italian Grand Prix because he "got done over" by Max Verstappen during the closing stages of qualifying at Monza. Russell appeared to be on course to live up to his status as pole favourite, but his final flying lap was compromised by Red Bull's Verstappen slowing down in front of him and his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli. Mercedes had placed championship leader Antonelli on track in front of Russell to give the Brit a tow, due to the fact the Italian is serving penalties for exceeding his engine-part allowance for the season and was going to start the race from the back of the grid regardless of his qualifying position.
